reasoning: For _fused_moe_kernel, SM throughput is 91.94% of peak while DRAM throughput is 42.12%; roofline also marks compute bottleneck (Compute SOL 91.9% vs Memory SOL 42.1%). Warps active are 100%, so the primary limit is arithmetic throughput, not occupancy or bandwidth.

root_causes.cause: Very high FP/VALU instruction pressure from fully fused FC1 + SiLU + FC2 loops dominates runtime.

evidence.interpretation: SM compute pipelines are close to peak, indicating compute saturation.

fixes.fix: Reduce instruction count per output by increasing tile reuse/unrolling efficiency (autotune BLOCK_J/BLOCK_OUT/num_warps and consider splitting fusion if it lowers redundant math).
fixes.rationale: When compute is saturated, speedup comes from fewer executed instructions per result or better instruction efficiency.

root_causes.cause: Kernel uses non-tensor-core path (VALU-heavy) for matrix-style work, limiting peak math throughput headroom.

evidence.interpretation: No tensor/matrix core utilization; math runs on standard vector ALUs.

fixes.fix: Refactor math to matrix-instruction/tensor-core-compatible formulation and datatypes where possible (or use Triton patterns that lower to MFMA on CDNA3).
fixes.rationale: Moving dense dot-product work to matrix engines can raise effective compute ceiling and reduce VALU bottleneck.
